```{r,echo=F,warning=F}
options(scipen=99)
P = sample(8:90,1)*100
n = sample(3:9,1)
r = round(runif(1,2,18),2)
sr = paste0(sprintf("%.2f",r),"%")

I = P*r*n/100

```

Question
========

If you invest a principal of \$`r P` into a **simple-interest** investment at an annual interest rate of `r sr` for a term of `r n` years, what will be your payout at the end of the term? 


Solution
========

The simple interest formula is $I=P\cdot r \cdot t$, where $P$ is the principal, $r$ is the annual interest rate in decimal form, and $t$ is time (in years).

$$I = `r P` \cdot `r r/100` \cdot `r n`$$


$$I = `r sprintf("%.2f",P*r*n/100)`$$

To find the total payout, add the interest to the principal.

$$T = P+I = `r sprintf("%.2f",P+I)`$$
